description:
STEP 2 (re-key on the arrow). Code-review finding 2. Captures (capture_tys ++ surface.inputs) are NOT part of the source arrow; ~50 sites slice .input positionally (capture/param split at runtime_demand.rs:1428-1434, callable_flow_resolutions builds inputs = capture_tys ++ surface.inputs at 1905-1941).

Model captures as LEADING addressed slots: a closure activation surface is (cap0..capK, param0..) -> r0, minted where the closure forms; the source contract arrow is the param SUFFIX. Replace every positional .input[i] / .input[..k] / .input[k..] consumer (~50, including the capture/param split) with structural projection BY ADDRESS (slot 1 <-> slot 1, no positional zip; addresses align the slots).

Re-verify the ~50 count and exact sites against HEAD before starting (runtime_demand.rs has moved since proposal authoring).

Depends on: re-key ActivationKey (fz-hwn.27.6).
Checks: closure/capture fixtures (Enum.reduce, nested direct-callable captures) stay green; capture/param split reads by address; no raw positional slice of .input survives. Lib + matrix green, zero warnings.

comments.text: Co-landing: not separable from 27.6 (proven empirically). Activation key inputs = capture_tys ++ surface.inputs, so the capture-slot model and the input re-key are the same change -- abi_ready_matches_direct_callable_captures_by_canonical_activation_key fails the moment inputs are re-keyed without it. See 27.6 finding.

title: Captures as leading addressed slots: replace positional .input slicing with structural projection
